task_name: MACE-MP-0 Foundation Model for Atomistic Materials Chemistry
scientific_goal: Develop and validate a universal foundation model for atomistic simulations that covers the periodic table, stably simulates diverse material systems, and achieves quantitative accuracy with minimal fine-tuning.

method_description.architecture: MACE (Message Passing Atomic Cluster Expansion) - higher-order equivariant message passing neural network with four-body messages, two message-passing layers, element embedding, and symmetric tensor product operations
method_description.training_data: MPTrj dataset from Materials Project (~1.6 million bulk crystals, DFT PBE+U level of theory, 89 chemical elements)
method_description.fine_tuning: Can be fine-tuned on just a handful of application-specific data points to reach ab initio accuracy

key_architectural_components: Two layers of message passing sufficient
Mildly nonlinear: only radial basis and final readout layer have nonlinear activations
Tensor decomposition for efficient parameterization of high body-order features

validation_experiments.name: Water RDF Simulation
validation_experiments.description: Liquid water structure via MD simulation

validation_experiments.name: Adsorption Energy Scaling Relations
validation_experiments.description: Scaling relations between O and OH adsorption energies on transition metal fcc(111) surfaces

validation_experiments.name: CRBH20 Reaction Barriers
validation_experiments.description: Reaction barrier comparison for three organic reactions

required_figures: Data overview: MPtrj dataset composition, periodic table coverage
Water RDF: O-O and O-H correlation functions vs experiment
Adsorption scaling relations: O vs OH binding energies on TM surfaces
Reaction barrier comparison: MACE vs DFT reference
